Alaska's FY2024 therefore reflects roughly 3.5 months of a combined entity rather than a full year, which affects scale comparisons and margin trend analysis (though it does not change the ranking below).

|---|---|---|

| American | $2,614M [DOC-1] | $846M [DOC-1] |
| Alaska | $570M [DOC-1] | $395M [DOC-1] |
| Southwest | $321M [DOC-1] | $465M [DOC-1] |

**Margins (derived from DOC-1 revenue and income figures):**

- Delta: 9.7% operating margin, 5.6% net margin ($5,995M / $3,457M on $61,643M revenue) [DOC-1]
- United: 8.9% operating margin, 5.5% net margin ($5,096M / $3,149M on $57,063M revenue) [DOC-1]
- American: 4.8% operating margin, 1.6% net margin ($2,614M / $846M on $54,211M revenue) [DOC-1]
- Alaska: 4.9% operating margin, 3.4% net margin ($570M / $395M on $11,735M revenue) [DOC-1]
- Southwest: 1.2% operating margin, 1.7% net margin ($321M / $465M on $27,483M revenue) [DOC-1]

**Conclusion.** Delta Air Lines was the most profitable on every measure — the largest operating income ($5,995M), the largest net income ($3,457M), and the highest operating and net margins [DOC-1]. United was a close second in both dollars and margin [DOC-1]. Southwest was the weakest operationally, with just $321M of operating income; its net income of $465M exceeded its operating income, indicating profitability supported by non-operating items rather than core operations [DOC-1].

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — highest FY2024 net income ($3,457M), operating income ($5,995M), and margins (5.6% net / 9.7% operating) of the five, with United second
